note: The closest match to the stated ICP anywhere in this batch and arguably in the corpus. 'Successful' — founder of a company he is currently building, Marine Corps reservist, former college athlete, owns 60 acres. 'Income' — recently bought a $10,000 tractor and another $10,000 item without ceremony, and confirmed the rep's read that 'the money is there'; the constraint he describes is startup cashflow timing and a psychological threshold about a single large outgoing, not means. 'Neglected_health' — no crisis anywhere, just five pounds a year of drift since marriage and kids, which is the criterion almost verbatim. 'Good_to_great' — the single best example of this criterion in the corpus: 'I'm not really that far off, I'm not in that bad of shape, I just want to get better, you know?' and 'I could reach my goals in like three months if I was dialed in.' 'Not_deconditioned' — emphatically; he trains almost daily, does pull-ups, EMOMs, rucking and competitive canoe racing. THE FINDING: this textbook-core prospect did not buy, and left the call actively comparing two other coaches against a $500/month anchor. Set against the existing assessments on file — where Robyn Stillwater, scored 'outside' on both occupation and income, closed at full price — the pattern now has evidence on both sides: ICP fit is not predicting purchase in either direction. The stated criteria describe the aspiration and, on this call, they also describe someone with a live competitive process, a firm reference price and no urgency, which are precisely the traits that make a well-qualified buyer hard to close. Worth noting too that the one thing that genuinely differentiated this prospect commercially — bilateral torn ACLs and a stated fear of joint replacement — is again invisible to the ICP, which still has no clinical criterion.
